title: Error Logging and Monitoring
description: Implement logging and monitoring for GraphQL errors to track issues in production.

data.text: Effective error logging and monitoring are essential for maintaining production GraphQL APIs. They help you identify issues, understand user problems, and improve API reliability.
Use the built-in logging integration in Hot Chocolate to log errors with structured data. The `IErrorLogger` interface allows you to customize error logging behavior.

data.title: Configure Error Logging
data.content: Set up structured error logging with Serilog.

data.text: Include context in your error logs such as user ID, request details, and error codes. This helps with debugging and analysis.

data.title: Enriched Error Logging
data.content: Add context to error logs for better debugging.

data.text: Integrate with Azure Application Insights or similar monitoring tools to track error rates, patterns, and performance metrics.

data.title: Application Insights Integration

data.text: Monitor error rates and set up alerts for unusual spikes. This helps you detect issues before they impact users significantly.

data.title: Don't Log Sensitive Data
data.text: Be careful not to log sensitive information like passwords, API keys, or personal user data in error logs. Sanitize error messages before logging.
Create dashboards to visualize error trends, top error codes, and affected operations. This helps you prioritize fixes and communicate issues to stakeholders.

data.title: Key Metrics to Track
data.code:
Metrics to monitor:
- Total error count
- Error rate (errors / total requests)
- Top 10 error codes
- Errors by operation/field
- Errors by user segment
- 95th percentile error response time
- Error trends over time

terms.definition: Hot Chocolate interface for intercepting and modifying errors before they are returned to the client.
Logging approach that includes context and metadata in a structured format for easier analysis.
Data about system performance and behavior used for monitoring and analysis.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use IErrorFilter to implement custom error logging
Include context like user ID and request ID in logs
Integrate with monitoring tools like Application Insights
Monitor error rates and set up alerts
Create dashboards to visualize error trends
Never log sensitive data in error messages
data.takeaway: You now have a complete error handling strategy with logging and monitoring for production GraphQL APIs.
